_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 10 Mathematical Literacy P2, November 2019 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Mathematical
Literacy questions hang off shared scenario boxes: the scenario (tables, graphs, plans and maps
described in bracketed words) is the 'context' of the first sub-question of each block and applies
to the sub-questions after it. memo_answer gives the guideline's working and final answer with
decimal commas kept; the guideline's mark codes (M method, A accuracy, CA consistent accuracy, RT
reading from table, C conclusion, O opinion, S simplification, R rounding) and level tags are left out.
FORMAT: 75 marks, 1½ hours, four compulsory questions (Q1 finance and measurement 26, Q2 measurement
13, Q3 maps 15, Q4 data handling and probability 21). An official ERRATA sheet issued with the paper
is tracked as paper2_errata.pdf; its amendments are
recorded in memo_note on 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 3.1.1, 3.2.1, 3.2.2, 4.1.1, 4.1.2 and 4.3.3. The marking guideline's running header reads 'EC/NOVEMBER 2018' but
its content is the 2019 Grade 10 P2 guideline.

subject: Mathematical Literacy

questions.context: QUESTION 1 | 1.1 Your friend, Kim, has asked you to help him with his bank statement. He is sure there are some errors on the bank statement as some things just do not make sense to him. Below is a copy of Kim's bank statement. [FIRST NATIONAL BANK statement for January 2019, Mr Kim de Villiers, 28 Nahoon Street, Nahoon 5241; account number 23456799, Vincent Park Branch, branch code 211021. Columns: Date | Details | Debit | Credit | Fees | Balance. Rows: 1/1/19 Opening balance | | | | 12 783,56; 3/1/19 Deposit | | 1 000,00 | 15,00 | 13 768,56; 5/1/19 Payment: Con Cars | 876,45 | | 2,50 | 12 889,61; 5/1/19 Payment: M Smith | 2 000,00 | | 2,50 | 10 887,11; 12/1/19 EFT Purchase | 125,60 | | 1,00 | A; 26/1/19 Payment: S Yusuf | 2 600,00 | | 2,50 | 8 158,01; 28/1/19 Salary | | 11 560,00 | | 19 718,01.] (NOTE: EFT means electronic funds transfer.) • The fee for deposits is R2,00 plus R1,00 for every R100,00. • Stop order payments cost R2,50 regardless of the amount. • Card purchases cost R1,00 regardless of the amount. • Rent is Kim's biggest expense. Use the above bank statement to answer the questions below.
questions.text: Determine the missing value of A.
Kim claims that there is a mistake in the fees column. Indicate where this mistake occurred and verify, with the necessary calculations, whether his statement is valid or not.
questions.memo_answer:
Deposit fee = R2,00 + R1,00 x (number of R100s)
Fee for 03/1/2019 = R2 + R1 x (R1 000 ÷ R100) = R2 + R10 = R12 (the statement shows R15)
The statement is valid.

questions.text: The bank has confirmed that there is indeed an error on his statement. If the error is corrected, what should Kim’s balance be on the 28 January 2019?

Kim states that her bank fees for January 2019 will be more than R30,00. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether his estimation is valid or not. Keep in mind that the error has been corrected.
questions.memo_answer:
Bank fees = R12 + R2,50 + R2,50 + R1,00 + R2,50 = R20,50
His statement is not correct.

questions.text: State ONE possible reason why banks are charging fees (to their customers).
questions.memo_answer:
So that they can do their daily operations
OR to be able to pay their employees
OR that is their way of getting an income
(accept other relevant reasoning)

questions.context: 1.2 Kim received an increase in his salary of 3,5% in April 2019. He wants to save his monthly increment and is planning to use it to build a concrete floor for his bird cage. [Pictures: concrete, wheelbarrow, bucket, cement.] Kim needs a concrete mixture of 0,27 cubic metres of cement, sand and gravel to make a concrete floor for his bird cage. He has a bucket with a capacity of 8 ℓ and a wheelbarrow with a capacity of 50 ℓ. Assume that 1 m³ = 1 000 litres.
questions.text: Calculate how much litres of concrete mixture will Kim need to build a floor for his cage.

The ratio of cement to sand to gravel is 1 : 3 : 5. How many litres of each cement, sand and gravel is needed? Assume that the volume of the concrete is more or less the same as the sum of the volumes of all the ingredients (cement, sand and gravel).
questions.memo_answer:
Ratio total = 1 + 3 + 5 = 9
Cement = 1/9 x 270 ℓ = 30 ℓ
Sand = 3/9 x 270 ℓ = 90 ℓ
Gravel = 5/9 x 270 ℓ = 150 ℓ

questions.text: Kim has asked Thato to do this work for him and he has agreed to do it on a Saturday. Calculate the amount of money Kim will have to pay Thato if the rate is R45,75 per hour (and part thereof) and he will finish the job in 5,4 hours. [NOTE: The rate is double on weekends.]
questions.memo_answer: Amount to be paid = R45,75 x (5 + 1) x 2 = R549

questions.text: The total cost for building material is R1 524,99, excluding labour. Kim saves his increment for six months. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether Kim will have enough money to start the project early in October 2019.
questions.memo_answer:
Total costs = R1 524,99 + R549 = R2 073,99
Total savings = (3,5% x R11 560) x 6 months = R2 427,60
Kim will have enough money for the project.

questions.context: QUESTION 2 | 2.1 Thembinkosi wants to put a trampoline in his yard as entertainment for his children. [Photograph: a round trampoline set into the ground in a garden.] The dimensions for the trampoline are shown below: [Diagram: a cylinder with diameter 4,3 m and height 90 cm.] He has started by digging a hole in order for the trampoline to be placed in the hole. Although Thembinkosi has used some of the dug-up sand, he has two-thirds of the sand left over. A company is prepared to collect the leftover sand free of charge, provided there is more than 5 m³ sand.
questions.text: Calculate the area of the base of the hole in square metres, rounded off to 2 decimal places. You may use the formula: Area = π r², where r = radius and π = 3,142
Determine, showing ALL calculations, whether there is enough sand for the company to come and collect it free of charge. You may use the formula: Volume = Area of base x height
questions.memo_answer:
Volume of the cylinder = 14,52 x 0,9 = 13,07 m³
2/3 x 13,07 = 8,71 m³
There is enough sand for it to be collected free of charge.

questions.context: 2.2 Thembinkosi has a backyard with an area of 929 m2.
questions.text: Thembinkosi has prepared a space of 3% of the area in his backyard for the construction of the trampoline. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether the prepared space will be enough or not.
questions.memo_answer:
Space prepared = 3% x 929 m² = 27,87 m²
Area of trampoline = 14,52 m²
He will have enough space.
questions.memo_note: Official errata (13 Nov 2019) also accepts: 14,52 ÷ 929 x 100 = 1,56% needed, therefore 3% will be sufficient.

questions.text: Thembinkosi currently pays R2 534 per month for insurance on his household. His broker told him that his insurance premium will go up by 2,5% after the trampoline has been installed. He predicts that his new monthly insurance premium will be R2 800. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether his statement is valid or not.
questions.memo_answer:
New premium = (2,5% x R2 534) + R2 534 = R2 597,35
His estimation is not correct.
questions.memo_note: Official errata also accepts: (2 800 - 2 534) ÷ 2 534 x 100 = 10,5% increase; statement is not valid.

questions.context: QUESTION 3 | Montego Pet Nutrition is a company that manufactures premium quality pet food that is distributed nationally and globally. The factory has undergone a R70 million-rand upgrade to its premises in Graaff-Reinet, Eastern Cape. [Road map of part of the Eastern Cape with a compass (N at the top) showing Graaff-Reinet, Pearston, Cradock, Somerset East, Jansenville, Wolwefontein, Glenconnor, Kariega, Kirkwood, Addo, Uitenhage, Despatch, Port Elizabeth, Humansdorp and Jeffrey's Bay; route R75 runs from Graaff-Reinet south-east through Jansenville, Wolwefontein and Kariega to Uitenhage and Port Elizabeth, with distances in km marked between towns.] Scale: 1 : 2 500 000 | 3.1
questions.text: Determine the shortest route, with a motor vehicle by road for delivering boxes of the pet food to the harbour in Port Elizabeth.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale and maps
questions.memo_answer: From Graaff-Reinet take the R75 route, passing Jansenville, Wolwefontein, Kariega and Uitenhage, until you reach Port Elizabeth (mention at least 2 towns).
questions.memo_note: Official errata: R75 only earns full marks; OR using map distances R75: 16+66+29+23+37+16+47+34 = 268 km, R63: 16+58+37+14+113+16+24+48 = 326 km, so the shortest route is the R75.

questions.text: In which direction would they travel from Graaff-Reinet to Port Elizabeth?
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale and maps
questions.memo_answer: South-east

questions.text: Why do you think the boxes are being delivered to the harbour in Port Elizabeth?
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale and maps
questions.memo_answer:
The boxes will be sent overseas.
OR any other logical reason.

questions.text: Use the number scale to determine the straight-line distance from Addo to Port Elizabeth. Give your answer in kilometres.
questions.topic: Maps and plans: scale and maps
questions.memo_answer:
Measured distance = 2 cm or 20 mm [accept 1,9-2,4 cm]
Actual distance = 2 x 2 500 000 = 5 000 000 cm ÷ 100 000 = 50 km
questions.memo_note: The guideline labels the measurement 'Distance from Addo to Uitenhage'; the question asks for Addo to Port Elizabeth, and the 50 km answer is the one used in 3.2.2. Official errata (distances changed in printing): accept 2,3 cm (2,1 cm-2,5 cm), OR Addo-PE = 72 km from the distances given on the map.

questions.text: The driver travels at a speed of 100 km/h and leaves Addo at 10h00. He predicts that he will reach Port Elizabeth at 10h55. Verify, with the necessary calculations, whether his statement is valid or not. Use the formula: Distance = speed × time
questions.memo_answer:
Time = distance ÷ speed = 50 km ÷ 100 km/h = 0,5 h = 30 min
His prediction is not valid; he will reach PE at 10:30.
questions.memo_note: Official errata, another option: distance = 100 km/h x (55 min ÷ 60) = 91,67 km travelled; not valid, he travelled further than 57,5 km (CA from 3.2.1).

questions.context: QUESTION 4 | 4.1 Mrs Base, a Mathematical Literacy teacher at Zinako High School, recorded the results of her Grade 10 learners in the final examination as a percentage, as shown below: 63 57 32 96 90 60 73 87 57 78 46 48 80 88 33 55 46 67 60 78 57 60 50 47 54 71 84 85 77 81
questions.text: Calculate the average mark of the Grade10 Mathematical Literacy learners in the final examination.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data
questions.memo_answer: Average = total of marks ÷ number of learners = 1 960 ÷ 30 = 65,33
questions.memo_note: Official errata: no penalty for rounding - accept 65,3 or 65.

questions.text: Mrs Base claims that the mode of the data will be 78%. Explain what the mode is and verify whether her statement is valid or not.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data
questions.memo_answer:
The mode is the number that appears the most in the data.
Mode = 57%, therefore her statement is invalid.
questions.memo_note: Official errata: the correct mode is 57% and 60%; do not penalise for not mentioning both modes.

questions.context: 4.2 Mrs Base's learners' performance in the examination is summarised in the table below. [TABLE 1: RATING CODE WITH SUMMARY OF LEARNERS' PERFORMANCE. Columns: Rating code | Description | Percentage | Number of learners. Rows: 7 Outstanding 80-100 A; 6 Meritorious 70-79 5; 5 Substantial 60-69 5; 4 Adequate 50-59 B; 3 Moderate 40-49 4; 2 Elementary 30-39 2; 1 Not achieved 0-29 0.]
questions.text: Determine the values of A and B.
questions.topic: Data handling: collecting, organising and summarising data

questions.text: What is the probability that a learner from Mrs Base’s Mathematical Literacy class scored less than 60% in final examinations? Write your answer as a percentage.

Pie chart 'Toilet facility': Flush toilets B, Bucket toilets 6%, No formal toilets 2%, Pit toilets 1%, Other 1%.] Refer to the pie charts above to answer the questions below.
questions.text: Determine the missing value of A and calculate how many semi-detached houses are in the Amathole District Municipality.

questions.topic: Data handling: representing and analysing graphs

questions.text: Give an example of the type of housing referred to as ‘other’ in the pie chart above.
